what_its_for: Metronidazole is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections. It is commonly used for infections of the stomach, intestines, vagina, skin, joints, and other areas of the body. Your doctor may also prescribe it for conditions like bacterial vaginosis, pelvic inflammatory disease, or certain stomach ulcers caused by H. pylori bacteria.
how_to_take: Take metronidazole exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush, chew, or break the extended-release tablets (Flagyl ER). If you are using the gel, cream, or lotion form, apply only to the affected skin area as directed. Wash your hands before and after applying. Do not use the skin gel near your eyes, nose, or mouth. Finish the entire course of medication even if you feel better, so the infection is fully treated.
dosing: The dose and how often you take metronidazole depends on the type of infection being treated. Common doses for adults range from 250 mg to 500 mg taken 2 to 3 times a day for 5 to 14 days. Your doctor will determine the right dose for you. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions on your prescription label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store metronidazole tablets and capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Store gels and creams as directed on the package, usually at room temperature. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking metronidazole and for at least 48 to 72 hours after your last dose. Mixing alcohol with metronidazole can cause a serious reaction including nausea, vomiting, flushing, fast heartbeat, and stomach cramps. Also avoid alcohol-containing products like mouthwash, cough syrups, and some sauces. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds, as metronidazole may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not have sexual intercourse while being treated for vaginal infections unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: seizures or convulsions, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, severe dizziness, vision changes, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, severe stomach pain or cramping, bloody or watery diarrhea, confusion or mood changes, painful or difficult urination, or dark or reddish-brown urine (this can be normal but check if unsure). Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting metronidazole. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of treatment even if you feel better sooner. Stopping too early can allow the infection to come back and may make it harder to treat. If you do not notice any improvement after 3 to 4 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Metronidazole should be used with caution during pregnancy, especially during the first trimester. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Breastfeeding: Metronidazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Metronidazole can be used in children but the dose will be adjusted based on weight. Always follow your pediatrician's instructions. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Use with care and follow your doctor's guidance. Liver disease: If you have liver problems, tell your doctor, as metronidazole is processed by the liver and your dose may need to be adjusted.
